reviewContext.issueReference: #184 (riela storage compact --help prints an internal helpRequested error instead of usage); workflowExecutionId opus-terra-design-and-implement-review-loop-session-542; design accepted by step3-design-review, plans accepted by step5-impl-plan-review (comm-010201, reviewDecision accept)
reviewContext.userProblem: riela storage compact --help/-h prints {"error":"helpRequested(...)"} and exits 1, and subcommands with required arguments (session status, workflow validate, ...) report a missing-argument error instead of printing usage.
requiredOutcomes: Any --help/-h token before -- prints the subcommand's existing usage on stdout with exit 0 and empty stderr, before required-argument checks, via one detector (CLIHelpRequest.detect) called first in RielaCLIApplication.runParsed.
Help text comes only from existing help texts (package/workflow run/workflow register/auth/worker/sandbox/gateway) or from usage lines in rielaCLIHelpText, falling back to the full help.
CleanExit is never reported as error JSON: StorageCommandFailure.result(_:usagePath:), RielaClientFamilyArguments.parseCLI and the runParsed final catch map it to help with exit 0.
Regression tests cover storage compact --help/-h, representative required-argument commands, a CLISurfaceEnumerator audit (excluding the delegated set and gateway <name>), and the backstops.
nonGoals: No new usage strings (kaiba/routine/version fall back to the full help).
No change to parse-level help returns in RielaArgumentParser, delegated runner help (gc, session prune, session reconcile, cache, environment) or native gateway <name> help.
No change to ad-hoc CLIUsageError(Self.message(for:)) wrappers other than RielaClientFamilyArguments.parseCLI.
No backward-compat overloads, no design-doc edits, no commit/push by workers.
constraints: Do not modify unrelated files; each plan edits only its writePaths.
Keep existing usage texts as the source of help output; do not invent divergent usage strings.
Run swift build/test/swiftlint from an arm64 shell (arch -arm64 /bin/zsh -lc) with focused swift test --filter suites.
Scratch files and logs go under tmp/issue-184/<planId>/.
designDecisionsAndRationale: D1: one detector at the top of RielaCLIApplication.runParsed, not per-parser help, so every subcommand gets uniform help before required-argument validation.
D2: help text only from existing producers or usage-line slices of rielaCLIHelpText, so help never diverges from documented usage.
D3: a help token before -- wins even in a value position; literal values use --opt=--help, matching existing contains(--help) checks and the --option=<value> rule for leading-dash values.
D4: delegated runners (gc, session prune, session reconcile, cache, environment) keep their ArgumentParser USAGE: output because they already handle help correctly.
§2.2: help is always plain text on stdout, exit 0, and ignores --output.
§2.4: CleanExit backstops in StorageCommandFailure.result, RielaClientFamilyArguments.parseCLI and the runParsed final catch, as defense in depth.
intentionalTradeoffs: kaiba, routine and version print the full top-level help instead of a dedicated usage (no new strings for #184).
Family-only help (e.g. workflow --help) prints the family's usage-line slice instead of the full help.
The usage-line slice depends on rielaCLIHelpText formatting.
Ad-hoc CLIUsageError wrappers are left as-is and rely on the detector, with the ch-01 audit test as coverage.
A W2 per-plan gate may end blocked-by-sibling; integrationVerification after the W2 join is authoritative.
supportedEdgeCases: Required-argument commands such as session status --help and workflow validate --help.
Help token in a value position (--message --help) is treated as help.
workflow run <target> --help keeps the run target for workflowRunHelpText(target:).
serve --help no longer starts a listener; auth invite --help no longer creates an invite.
Unmatched full path falls back by dropping the last word (events validate -> events usage line).
outOfScopeEdgeCases: riela --help / -h / bare riela keep the existing top-level help.
Unknown first token keeps the unknown-command error.
gateway <name> ... (name != list) keeps the gateway's native --help.
